sources.entry: tty7 - A GPU-rendered, daemon-backed terminal in pure Rust with sessions that stay alive without tmux. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/tty7) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
tty7 - A GPU-rendered, daemon-backed terminal in pure Rust; sessions survive quitting the app without tmux.

summary.one_liner: tty7 is a GPU-rendered terminal workbench written in pure Rust, where a background server keeps shells and panes alive across app quits and reboots without tmux.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a background server that owns shells and panes, so quitting the window leaves sessions running; after a reboot, layout, screen contents, and supported agent conversations are restored. It renders on Zed's gpui and uses the VT core from Alacritty. It detects 28 AI coding CLIs (such as Claude Code and Codex) per pane, showing status, notifications, and git branch and diff, and can be installed with hooks for status and resume. It ships a bundled tty7 CLI that lets agents open panes, send input, wait, and capture output. Other features include shell integration for zsh, bash, fish, PowerShell and WSL, a side panel with process tree, file tree, diffs and GitHub issues/PRs via gh, and remote workspaces over a native SSH stack with SFTP and port forwarding. The README includes a self-reported benchmark against Alacritty, Ghostty, and Kitty.
use_cases: keep terminal sessions running after closing the app
monitor multiple AI coding agents across repos
remote development over SSH from a local terminal
let one AI agent drive panes for another
terminal with built-in autosuggestions and history search
how_to_run: Download the native build for macOS, Windows, or Linux from the Releases page
macOS: open the .dmg and drag into Applications
Linux: chmod +x the AppImage and run it
Optional: npx skills add l0ng-ai/tty7 to install the agent skill
notable: Background server owns shells so sessions survive quitting the app, with no tmux needed
Per-pane detection and status for 28 AI coding CLIs, with past sessions listed in search
Agents can script the terminal via a bundled CLI (run, split, send, wait, capture)
Remote workspaces where files, repos and git data stay on the remote machine
Self-reported benchmark claiming about 2x Alacritty throughput
caveats: Benchmark figures are self-reported by the author and measured on one machine (Apple M1 Pro, macOS)
Agent status, notifications and resume require installing per-agent hooks under Settings → Integrations
Prebuilt installers are listed for macOS, Windows and Linux; README does not describe build-from-source steps
